notes: RAISE BY YEAR, IN RATES & ASSUMPTIONS AND IN SCENARIOS. Salary growth was one rate plus each person's appraisal month. It is now one function, salaryGrowthFn in runProjection: the default for every year, overridden by raise-schedule rows. Each row has From year, To year, Raise % and the month the raise first shows in pay. 0% skips a year, for a job switch. A From-To range covers a new appraisal cycle, e.g. 10% every July from 2028. Later rows win on overlap. A raise landing on or before the plan start is already in the entered salary and is not counted. Years without a row use the old hikesForMonth rule exactly, so with no rows every number is byte-identical to before; verified against v2026.05.13.03. RATES & ASSUMPTIONS: a 'raise by year' table per person under the appraisal month, saved with Apply into state.raiseSchedule.{p1,p2}. New rows are pre-filled with next year and the default rate and month. SCENARIOS: the Salaries group in Change my plan has 'Name . Annual raise' per person with the same four inputs. Scenario raise rows layer on the base schedule and win on overlap. A new-salary row in the same scenario grows by that schedule, through salaryPathFor, the one function both the engine and the editor default use. Example verified: Salary 3,00,000 from 2027-03, raise 2027 0%, raise 2028-2080 10% from July gives 3,00,000 to Jun 28, 3,30,000 from Jul 28, 3,63,000 from Jul 29. Engine attribution keeps rows additive: each scenario's raise rows, then each salary revision; the rows sum to the income change in every month. Sabbatical and retirement scale them like the base; recorded-salary months and retirement stops still win. FIXED WHILE BUILDING: applyRevisions returned early when a scenario had no amount changes, so a scenario holding only raise rows did nothing. Editor: switching a row between an amount item and Annual raise rebuilds its inputs; typed values in other rows survive. The line under a raise row compares the plan's raise for that year with yours, and warns if it lands before the plan start. The Rates table wraps on narrow screens (measured at 390px and 1280px: no overlap, no overflow). VERIFIED in headless Chromium: 16 schedule and job-switch engine checks; 17 browser checks driving the Rates tab via its nav item (add, edit, Apply, sheet values, delete back to identical) and the scenario editor (dropdown, rebuild, defaults, line text, save, summary, preview showing 2,00,000, 3,00,000, 3,00,000, 3,00,000, 3,30,000, 3,63,000 marked, reopen, switch back); all earlier suites pass; no page errors. FLAGGED, NOT CHANGED: the toggle 'Grow investment contributions with salary' says contributions scale at the salary rate, but the engine has always grown them at the EXPENSE rate and month. Raise-by-year rows therefore do not affect contributions. NOT VERIFIED: the guards sheetVsDash, decisionUsesChain, instrumentCrossPageMismatch and accountDeltaMismatches are not in the HTML file and were not run. NOT BUILT: closed-EMI zero row; settlement on its own line; Edit balances port and Instruments page deletion; Decisions/Scenarios merge.
